ops.title: cc-interact v0.31.1: DAEMONKIT_HOME test seam + releases/latest repaired; 43 tags still lack release objects
ops.body:
Released 2026-07-27. Tag v0.31.1 -> 1c5c50c6c9a1b7aeacbbaf350017a9236b4811ec, pins daemonkit v0.20.9.

## Test sandbox seam

daemonkit v0.20.9 resolves every home-derived durable path through the passwd
database and ignores $HOME (daemonkit internal/realhome). Every existing
`t.Setenv("HOME", dir)` therefore stopped sandboxing the suite, and a bumped
tree wrote into the real home directory.

The seam is the env var `DAEMONKIT_HOME`, read by name at runtime. Because
daemonkit's `realhome.EnvOverride` constant lives under `internal/`, consumers
must spell the string. cc-interact's `internal/testhome` does that:
`Set(t, dir)` sets HOME and DAEMONKIT_HOME to the same dir; `Isolate(t)` uses a
fresh `t.TempDir()`. All 24 former HOME sites across 9 test files call it.
HOME stays set alongside because non-daemonkit code still reads it.

Three sites pass a short `/tmp` dir instead of `t.TempDir()` (unix socket
`sun_path` limit on macOS): channel/connectivity_test.go, cmd/cmd_test.go,
daemon/server_test.go `shortHome`. Those call `testhome.Set`.

Verification: full `go test -race -count=1 -p 2 ./...` green under an outer
`DAEMONKIT_HOME=/tmp/w2-cc-interact-gate` pollution guard, and the guard
directory stayed EMPTY — every per-test seam held, nothing fell back to it.
Never export DAEMONKIT_HOME process-wide: cc-orchestrate's install-binary.sh
uses the same name with a different meaning.

## Local flake, not a repo defect

Under load average ~72 (concurrent agent fleet on this Mac), the daemonkit
trust verifier child spawn times out and the daemon readiness probe's 5s
deadline expires: seen as `trust: run verifier child: worker: timed out` in
cmd and `daemon did not become ready ... i/o timeout` in channel, on different
tests across runs. Each package passes alone, and `-p 2` clears the whole
suite. daemonkit v0.20.6..v0.20.9 has zero diff under trust/, worker/, proc/,
so this is not a pin regression.

## Release-object debt (NOT backfilled)

Before this release, releases/latest pointed at v0.30.1 while v0.31.0 and
v0.30.0 were newer tags with green Release runs and no release object.
`gh release create v0.31.1 --latest` repaired the pointer.

The Release workflow is npm-only (publishes @cc-interact/react, skipping
versions already on npm); it never creates a GitHub release object. Every
release object in this repo was made by hand, which is why the set is sparse.
43 of 47 tags have no release object:

v0.1.1-v0.1.10, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0, v0.6.0, v0.7.0, v0.7.1, v0.8.0,
v0.9.0, v0.9.1, v0.10.0, v0.11.0, v0.11.1, v0.12.0, v0.13.0, v0.14.0,
v0.15.0, v0.16.0, v0.16.1, v0.17.0, v0.18.0, v0.18.1, v0.19.0, v0.20.0,
v0.21.0, v0.22.0, v0.24.0, v0.25.0, v0.30.0, v0.31.0.

Tags that DO have one: v0.1.0, v0.23.0, v0.26.0-v0.29.0, v0.30.1, v0.31.1.

Deliberately left alone per the release instruction. If the sparseness ever
matters, the durable fix is teaching .github/workflows/release.yml to create
the release object from the CHANGELOG entry, not a one-off backfill.
